correctness.rationale: Fully explicit: reprojected two-node Lanczos exactly computes the bilinear inverse of a 2x2 SPD compression. Polar Gaussian separation yields two angular integrals, with the second obtained by differentiating the first; E[R²]=2 and E[R⁴]=8. From these the first and second moments, variance difference, squared bias, and if-and-only-if MSE thresholds follow algebraically. All eigenvalue and breakdown boundaries are stated, and 1,694 independent numerical/symbolic-identity checks passed.

value.rationale: The motivating P-SLQ algorithm makes a real design choice between quadrature depth and number of probes at a fixed product budget. This theorem exactly settles that choice (including strict and equality regimes) on the natural final two-dimensional unresolved complement. Its variance reversal shows why more accurate individual quadrature does not necessarily yield lower trace MSE under tight budgets. This is a sharp natural numerical-allocation invariant, rather than a parameter rename or a standalone software experiment; it does not pretend to be a general large-dimensional theorem.
